title: Home Mortgage Loans: Loan Approval, Note Rate, Closing and Escrow Election
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Loan Approval, Note Rate, Closing and Escrow Election

This policy governs how a loan under Home Mortgage Loans moves from an approved application to a funded loan in servicing: who decides approval, which rate the note carries, how the proceeds are paid out, when the first installment is owed, and whether escrow can be declined.

## Clauses

**Approval.** A loan is approved only if it falls inside every limit of its program: the smallest and largest loan amount, the maximum loan-to-value, the minimum credit score, the maximum debt-to-income ratio and the list of eligible occupancy types. Approval is a credit decision taken by the underwriting system. A support agent never makes it, whether to grant or to refuse.

**Note rate.** The note rate is the program's par rate, locked for the program's lock period.

**Funding.** At closing the loan funds through one single disbursement. Where the program finances an upfront insurance premium or funding fee, that premium is part of the same disbursement. Funding moves the loan from applied to active, and from then on the bank services it. The original property value kept for the loan is the lower of the appraised value and the purchase price at origination.

**First installment.** The first installment is owed on the program's due day, in the month reached by counting the program's first-due offset in calendar months past the month in which the loan funded.

**Escrow.** Escrow is compulsory where the program marks it as always required, and also where the original loan-to-value is above the program's escrow threshold. In every other case the borrower may decline escrow by paying, at closing, the program's waiver fee, expressed as a percentage of the loan amount.

**Applications that end without a loan.** An application that is denied or withdrawn ends in withdrawn status; the same status results when a loan does not close inside its funding window.

## Escrow election as a decision table

| Program's escrow setting | Original loan-to-value compared with the program threshold | Result |
|---|---|---|
| always required | not relevant | escrow is compulsory |
| a percentage threshold | above the threshold | escrow is compulsory |
| a percentage threshold | at or below the threshold | the borrower may waive escrow by paying the waiver fee at closing |

## Points of judgement

**May an agent tell a caller that an application is approved because the figures fit the program limits?** No. Fitting the limits is necessary, but the approval itself belongs to the underwriting system.

**Is a financed premium paid out separately from the loan proceeds?** No; the loan funds with one disbursement that already contains it.

**Illustration of a single disbursement (imagined figures).** With an imagined base loan amount of $300000.00 and an imagined financed premium of 2 percent of the base amount, the premium is $6000.00 and the one disbursement at closing is $306000.00. The 2 percent rate is chosen only to show the arithmetic and is not the rate of any program.
